findings.excerpt: private theorem coordEquiv_x (e : k ≃+* k') : coordEquiv q e (DrinfeldCurve.x q k) = DrinfeldCurve.x q k' := by
findings.problem: The four `coordEquiv` computation lemmas are the canonical rewrite rules for `coordEquiv q e`: on `mk p`, on `algebraMap a`, on `x` and on `y`. They are plain private theorems, not `@[simp]`. `coordEquiv` is a private def, so simp cannot see through it. Every use therefore needs a hand-ordered `rw` chain, for example `rw [hφ, hψ, DrinfeldPhi.coordEquiv_x]` (lines 131–132), `rw [h1, h2, coordEquiv_mk, MvPolynomial.map_C]` (line 41) and the chain at line 145. The proofs of `coordEquiv_x` and `coordEquiv_y` also have to unfold `x` and `y` manually. These rules do not overlap. Their left-hand sides have distinct heads: `mk`, `algebraMap`, `x`, `y`. `coordEquiv_mk` rewrites to `MvPolynomial.map`, which already has simp lemmas, so a simp set would terminate.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `coordEquiv_mk`, `coordEquiv_algebraMap`, `coordEquiv_x` and `coordEquiv_y` as `@[simp]`. Private simp lemmas are allowed. Also make `coordEquiv_mk` the rewrite used for `x` and `y` (they unfold to `mk (X _)`). Then `coordEquiv_x` and `coordEquiv_y` become `by simp [DrinfeldCurve.x]` and the `solution` bullets reduce to `simp [hφ, hψ]`-style calls. As an alternative, add a `@[simp]` `coordEquiv_apply` that exposes the underlying `Ideal.quotientEquiv`, so the `show … rfl` steps disappear.
findings.benefit: Callers get a normal form for `coordEquiv` applied to `mk`, `x`, `y` and constants without remembering which lemma to rewrite with, and the ordering-sensitive `rw` chains go away. Later results that push `coordEquiv` through coordinate-ring expressions can use plain `simp`.

findings.excerpt: rw [hFunctionFieldAction_algebraMap, hφ, hφ, hFunctionFieldAction_algebraMap, hψ, DrinfeldPhi.coordEquiv_hAction]
findings.problem: The equivariance goal is closed with a rewrite chain whose order matters, and `hφ` has to be used twice. The pieces are not available to simp. `hFunctionFieldAction_algebraMap` in Definitions/Def_DrinfeldCurve_FunctionField.lean is not `@[simp]`, although it is the only way to compute `hFunctionFieldAction … (algebraMap _ _ a)`. `hφ` is a local `have` for `IsFractionRing.ringEquivOfRingEquiv_algebraMap`, which Mathlib does not mark `@[simp]` (only `apply` is generated by `simps!`). `coordEquiv_hAction` is not simp either. The user had to hand-write `simp only [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.coe_coe]` followed by this ordered rewrite.
findings.proposed_change: In Def_DrinfeldCurve_FunctionField.lean, tag `hFunctionFieldAction_algebraMap` with `@[simp]`. Its right-hand side is an `algebraMap` of an element of a smaller type, so it normalises toward the coordinate ring and cannot cycle. Add `hφ` to the local simp set. Then close the bullet with `simp [hφ, hψ, DrinfeldPhi.coordEquiv_hAction]`. Do not change the Mathlib attribute. Pass `hφ` explicitly, or tag a local copy.
findings.benefit: The statement `φ ∘ hFunctionFieldAction = hFunctionFieldAction ∘ φ` on `algebraMap` generators becomes a one-line `simp` for this and other function-field results. The proof no longer depends on the order and multiplicity of rewrites.

findings.excerpt: simp [MvPolynomial.mapEquiv_apply, drinfeldPoly, map_sub, map_mul, map_pow, MvPolynomial.map_X, map_one]
findings.problem: The simp argument list repeats lemmas that are already in the default simp set: `MvPolynomial.mapEquiv_apply`, `MvPolynomial.map_X`, `map_sub`, `map_mul`, `map_pow` and `map_one`. Only `drinfeldPoly` is needed. A similar pattern appears in `map_substPoly`, which lists `MvPolynomial.map_X` and `RingHom.coe_coe` twice in one `simp only`. The long lists hide which lemma matters and suggest the simp interface is not being relied on.
findings.proposed_change: Reduce to `simp [drinfeldPoly]`. In the `simp only` calls in `map_substPoly`, drop the duplicated `MvPolynomial.map_X` and `RingHom.coe_coe`. I have not compiled this change.
findings.benefit: A reader sees that only unfolding `drinfeldPoly` is needed. The proof does not break if these lemmas are later reorganised.
